# Apple ARM64 ordinary-header A/A score window v2

The v1 experiment stopped before warmup when the global Pageouts count increased from 795 to 916 across untimed setup. Swapouts stayed at zero. The published v1 gate applied from before setup, so [run 45933978291](https://github.com/Sugarchain-CI/sugarchain-en/actions/runs/45933978291) remains inconclusive. It produced no warmup or scored timings.

XNU reports Pageouts and compressor Swapouts separately. The vnode pager can write back dirty file-backed pages with a pageout flag, which increments Pageouts when the qualifying pages are cleaned. The explicit msync path uses a separate flag. These paths explain how Pageouts can increase with no compressor Swapouts. The v1 receipt cannot identify the source of its 121 pages. [Host counters](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/xnu-11215.81.4/osfmk/kern/host.c#L140-L153), [vnode requests](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/xnu-11215.81.4/bsd/vm/vnode_pager.c#L401-L407), [UPL flags](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/xnu-11215.81.4/bsd/kern/ubc_subr.c#L2596-L2610), [pageout accounting](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/xnu-11215.81.4/osfmk/vm/vm_upl.c#L1108-L1115)

One v2 run measures the same two copies of the retained, independently verified native CLI artifact from run 45929559984. It uses private datadirs and the same genuine early Mainnet headers, setup work floor, native host class, process CPU accounting and 480-second runtime budget. The two warmup pairs and 12 scored pairs keep the v1 AB/BA order, exact payloads, accepted index and chainwork checks, inactive-process CPU bounds and combined 3 GiB footprint bound.

The schema-2 receipt records host counters before setup, after each node reaches the work floor and after each warmup. After both warmups complete, capture host counters and both live process snapshots, request one five-second sleep with no new peer or RPC work, and capture both again. Require at least five elapsed seconds with no changes in host Pageouts or Swapouts and at most 50 ms of CPU per daemon. Check the footprint cap at both endpoints. Record any failure and all unstarted trials. Use the post-quiet snapshot as the explicit score baseline.

Require zero change in both host counters after every scored pair. Keep all scheduled arms and captured data. Passing still requires at least 11 pairs within 2.5% wall and 0.5% CPU, all 12 within 5% wall and 1% CPU, and both order-median separations within the near bounds. A diagnostic failure is inconclusive. A fully measured margin failure stays failed. This protocol is a single score-window calibration and has no retry on either outcome.

This diagnostic measures paired timing noise on one hosted machine. It does not qualify the earlier rejected ordinary-header candidate, estimate end-to-end Mainnet sync time or alter product code.
